gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.0: In order to use monitors, you have to split them into groups first. A group may only have 1 module in it.

gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.2: Then in the settings page for the group you can insert a module, you can configure it in the same page.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.3: To delete a group, select all of it's components and click 'Remove from group'.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.4: You can quickly select all components of a group by clicking on it's name. Click again to unselect.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.5: Some modules may display things depending on the block they target, to set a target for a group select any component of that group and right-click on the target component.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.6: You may wish to select a target that is not in the multiblock, you have to use the wireless transmitter cover for that.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.7: Place the cover on the target block, right-click it with a data stick and put that data stick into a data access hatch in the multiblock.
gtpm.central_monitor.info_tooltip.8: Then select the data access hatch as the target, and set the slot index of your data stick in the number field that appeared.

gtpm.multiblock.assembly_line.descriptio: The Assembly Line is a large multiblock structure consisting of 5 to 16 "slices". In theory, it's large Assembling Machine, used for creating advanced crafting components.

This is a machine that monitors machines proxied by the Digital Interface Cover. You can easily monitor the Fluids, Items, Energy, and States of machines proxied in Energy Network.
You can build the central monitor screen from 3X2 to %dX%d (width X height).
The default height is 3. You can adjust the screen height in the GUI before the structure is formed.
Energy consumption: %d EU/s for each screen.
gtpm.multiblock.charcoal_pile.descriptio: Converts logs into Brittle Charcoal in a 9x4x9 area beneath it.
The floor of the pit must be made from bricks, and any ground-related block can be used for the walls and roof. No air can be inside the pit.
Larger pits take more time to process logs, but are more efficient.
gtpm.multiblock.coke_oven.description: The Coke Oven is a multiblock structure used for getting coke and creosote in the early game. It doesn't require fuel and has an internal tank of 32 buckets for creosote. Its inventory can be accessed via its Coke Oven Hatch.
gtpm.multiblock.computation.non_bridging: A Reception Hatch is linked to a machine which cannot bridge
gtpm.multiblock.cracker.description: The Oil Cracking Unit is a multiblock structure used for turning Light and Heavy Fuel into their Cracked variants.
gtpm.multiblock.data_bank.description: The Data Bank is a multiblock structure used for sharing Assembly Line Research Data between multiple Assembly Lines. Additionally, it enables Assembly Lines to read more complex research data on Data Modules.
gtpm.multiblock.distillation_tower.descr: The Distillation Tower is a multiblock structure used for distilling the various types of Oil and some of their byproducts. Each layer must have exactly one output hatch, starting from the second one. The bottom layer can output items and insert fluids in any position.
gtpm.multiblock.electric_blast_furnace.d: The Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) is a multiblock structure used for smelting alloys, cooking metals and refining ores. It is required for obtaining high-tier alloys and metals, such as aluminium, stainless steel, titanium, and naquadah alloy.
gtpm.multiblock.extreme_combustion_engin: The Extreme Combustion Engine is a multiblock structure that acts as a Combustion Generator for IV power.
gtpm.multiblock.hpca.description: The High Performance Computing Array (HPCA) is a multiblock structure used for creating Compute Work Units (CWU/t) for more complex Assembly Line Research Data. The structure has a flexible 3x3 area which can be filled in any way with HPCA components. Different components can provide different amounts of Computation, Cooling, as well as Energy Cost, Coolant Cost, and Heat Production. When used with a Bridge Component, the HPCA can connect to Network Switches for combining and routing Computation from multiple sources to one or more destinations.
gtpm.multiblock.hpca.error_temperature: Temperature above 100C, components may be damaged!
gtpm.multiblock.hpca.warning_multiple_br: - Multiple bridges in structure (provides no additional benefit)
gtpm.multiblock.hpca.warning_temperature: Temperature above 50C, components may be damaged at 100C!
gtpm.multiblock.implosion_compressor.des: The Implosion Compressor is a multiblock structure that uses explosives to turn gem dusts into their corresponding gems.
gtpm.multiblock.invalid_structure.toolti: This block is a controller of the multiblock structure. For building help, see structure template in JEI.
gtpm.multiblock.large_boiler.description: Large Boilers are multiblocks that generate steam from an energy source and water. Said energy source is either any Solid Fuel with a Burn Time, or a Diesel/Semi-Fluid Fuel. Can be throttled back in increments of 5%% to reduce Steam output and Fuel consumption.
gtpm.multiblock.large_boiler.explosion_t: Will explode if provided Fuel with no Water
gtpm.multiblock.large_boiler.throttle.to: Boiler can output less Steam and consume less fuel (efficiency is not lost, does not affect heat-up time)
gtpm.multiblock.large_chemical_reactor.d: The Large Chemical Reactor performs chemical reactions at 100%% energy efficiency. Overclocks multiply both speed and energy by 4. The multiblock requires exactly 1 Cupronickel Coil Block, which must be placed adjacent to the PTFE Pipe casing located in the center.
§bUpgrade the Dynamo Hatch to enable Oxygen Boosting.
The Large Combustion Engine is a multiblock structure that acts as a Combustion Generator for EV power.
gtpm.multiblock.large_turbine.descriptio: Large Turbines are multiblocks that generate power from steam, gases, and plasma by having them spin the turbine's rotor. Energy output is based on rotor efficiency and current speed of turbine. Gearbox casings are used in the center of the structure.
gtpm.multiblock.luv_fusion_reactor.descr: The Fusion Reactor MK 1 is a large multiblock structure used for fusing elements into heavier ones. It can only use LuV, ZPM, and UV Energy Hatches. For every Hatch it has, its buffer increases by 10M EU, and has a maximum of 160M.
gtpm.multiblock.max_energy_per_tick_hove: The maximum EU/t available for running recipes or overclocking
gtpm.multiblock.max_recipe_tier_hover: The maximum tier of recipes that can be run
gtpm.multiblock.monitor_screen.tooltip.0: The GUI can be opened with a right-click of a screwdriver.
gtpm.multiblock.monitor_screen.tooltip.1: The proxy mode of Digital Interface Cover can delegate machines' capabilities and GUI. (Yes, you can connect pipes directly on the screen.)
gtpm.multiblock.multi_furnace.descriptio: The Multi Smelter is a multiblock structure used for smelting massive amounts of items at once. Different tiers of coils provide a speed boost and energy efficiency gain. 32 is the base value of items smelted per operation, and can be multiplied by using higher level coils.
gtpm.multiblock.multiple_recipemaps.head: Machine Mode:
gtpm.multiblock.multiple_recipemaps.swit: The machine must be off to switch modes!
gtpm.multiblock.multiple_recipemaps.tool: Screwdriver the controller to change which machine mode to use.
gtpm.multiblock.network_switch.descripti: The Network Switch is a multiblock structure used for distributing Computation from many sources to many destinations. It can accept any number of Computation Data Reception or Transmission Hatches. It is necessary for Research Data which requires much higher Computation, as the Research Station can only accept one Computation Data Reception Hatch. HPCAs must have a Bridge Component for the Network Switch to be able to access their Computation.

The Primitive Blast Furnace (PBF) is a multiblock structure used for cooking steel in the early game. Although not very fast, it will provide you with steel for your first setups.
gtpm.multiblock.primitive_water_pump.des: The Primitive Water Pump is a pre-Steam Era multiblock that collects water once per second, depending on the Biome it is in. It can use a Pump, ULV, or LV Output Hatch, increasing the amount of water per tier. Follows the formula: Biome Coefficient * Hatch Multiplier.
gtpm.multiblock.primitive_water_pump.ext: While raining in the Pump's Biome, the total water production will be increased by 50%%.
gtpm.multiblock.pyrolyse_oven.descriptio: The Pyrolyse Oven is a multiblock structure used for turning Logs into Charcoal and Creosote Oil, or Ash and Heavy Oil.
gtpm.multiblock.research_station.descrip: The Research Station is a multiblock structure used for researching much more complex Assembly Line Research Data. Any Research requiring a Data Orb or Data Module must be scanned in the Research Station. Requires Compute Work Units (CWU/t) to research recipes, which is supplied by High Performance Computing Arrays (HPCAs).
gtpm.multiblock.steam.duration_modifier: Takes §f1.5x §7base duration to process, not affected by number of items.
gtpm.multiblock.steam_grinder.descriptio: A Multiblock Macerator at the Steam Age. Requires at least 14 Bronze Casings to form. Cannot use normal Input/Output busses, nor Fluid Hatches other than the Steam Hatch.
gtpm.multiblock.steam_oven.description: A Multi Smelter at the Steam Age. Requires at least 6 Bronze Casings to form. Cannot use normal Input/Output busses, nor Fluid Hatches other than the Steam Hatch. Steam Hatch must be on the bottom layer, no more than one.
gtpm.multiblock.title: Multiblock Pattern
gtpm.multiblock.turbine.efficiency_toolt: Each Rotor Holder above %s§7 adds §f10%% efficiency and multiplies EU/t by 2§7.
gtpm.multiblock.universal.distinct.info: If enabled, each Item Input Bus will be treated as fully distinct from each other for recipe lookup. Useful for things like Programmed Circuits, Extruder Shapes, etc.
gtpm.multiblock.universal.has_problems_h: Fix the following issues in a Maintenance Hatch:
gtpm.multiblock.universal.muffler_obstru: Muffler Hatch must have a block of airspace in front of it.
gtpm.multiblock.uv_fusion_reactor.descri: The Fusion Reactor MK 3 is a large multiblock structure used for fusing elements into heavier ones. It can only use UV Energy Hatches. For every Hatch it has, its buffer increases by 40M EU, and has a maximum of 640M.
gtpm.multiblock.vacuum_freezer.descripti: The Vacuum Freezer is a multiblock structure mainly used for freezing Hot Ingots into regular Ingots. However, it can also freeze other substances, such as Water.
gtpm.multiblock.zpm_fusion_reactor.descr: The Fusion Reactor MK 2 is a large multiblock structure used for fusing elements into heavier ones. It can only use ZPM and UV Energy Hatches. For every Hatch it has, its buffer increases by 20M EU, and has a maximum of 320M.

gtpm.oc.tooltip.2: Right click to decrease the OC
gtpm.oc.tooltip.3: Middle click to reset the OC
gtpm.oc.tooltip.4: Hold Shift to change by Perfect OC
gtpm.placeholder_info.active.0: Returns a 1 if the block the cover is attached to is currently running a recipe, 0 otherwise.
gtpm.placeholder_info.active.2: {active} -> whether there's a currently running recipe
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.0: Returns information about auto-crafting in the ME network of the block this cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.10: {ae2crafting get <index> time} -> the amount of time elapsed from the start of the craft (in nanoseconds), or 0 if the CPU is idle
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.2: {ae2crafting get amount} -> the amount of crafting CPUs in the ME network
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.3: {ae2crafting get <index> storage} -> the amount of crafting storage the specified CPU has
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.4: {ae2crafting get <index> threads} -> the amount of co-processors the specified CPU has
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.5: {ae2crafting get <index> name} -> the name of the specified crafting CPU
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.6: {ae2crafting get <index> selectionMode} -> the selection mode of the specified crafting CPU (used for manual, automatic or both requests)
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.7: {ae2crafting get <index> amount} -> the amount of the item that was requested, or 0 if the CPU is idle
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.8: {ae2crafting get <index> item} -> the display name of the item that was requested, or 0 if the CPU is idle
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2crafting.9: {ae2crafting get <index> progress} -> the crafting job progress, or 0 if the CPU is idle
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2energy.0: Returns the energy currently stored in the ME network of the block this cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2energy.2: {ae2energy} -> the energy in the ME network (in AE units)
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2fluidCount.0: Same as fluidCount, but counts items in the ME network of the block this cover is attached to.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2fluidCount.1: Note that counting all fluids may cause lag!
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2fluidCount.3: {fluidCount [fluidId]} -> the amount of all fluids, or the fluid with fluidId if specified
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2itemCount.0: Same as itemCount, but counts items in the ME network of the block this cover is attached to.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2itemCount.1: Note that counting by filter or all items may cause lag!
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2itemCount.4: {itemCount <item_id>} -> amount of items with ids equal to item_id
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2itemCount.5: {itemCount filter <slot_id>} -> amount of items matching filter in specified slot of this cover
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2maxPower.0: Returns the energy capacity of the ME network of the block this cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2maxPower.2: {ae2maxPower} -> the energy capacity of the ME network
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2powerUsage.0: Returns the energy consumption of the ME network of the block this cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2powerUsage.2: {ae2powerUsage} -> the energy consumption of the ME network
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2spatial.0: Returns information about spatial I/O in the ME network of the block this cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2spatial.2: {ae2spatial power} -> the amount of power required to initiate spatial I/O
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2spatial.3: {ae2spatial efficiency} -> the efficiency of the Spatial Containment Structure (SPS)
gtpm.placeholder_info.ae2spatial.4: {ae2spatial size<X|Y|Z>} -> the size of the SPS along the specified axis (example: 'Size: {sizeX}x{sizeY}x{sizeZ}')
gtpm.placeholder_info.amperage.0: Returns the amperage in the wire/cable the cover is on.
gtpm.placeholder_info.blockNbt.0: Returns the NBT of the block entity
gtpm.placeholder_info.bufferText.0: Returns the text from a buffer accessible by ComputerCraft
gtpm.placeholder_info.bufferText.2: {bufferText <line>} -> text from the buffer on the specified line (line is 1-100)
gtpm.placeholder_info.calc.0: Returns the result of a math function or operation.
gtpm.placeholder_info.calc.3: {calc <round|floor|ceil|sqrt|~> <arg>} -> the result of the specified operation
gtpm.placeholder_info.calc.4: {calc <first_arg> <+|-|*|/|//|>>|<<|%> <second_arg>} -> the result of the specified operation
gtpm.placeholder_info.click.0: Returns whether the targeted advanced monitor was clicked before the current tick
gtpm.placeholder_info.click.2: {click} -> "1" if the targeted advanced monitor was clicked, "0" otherwise
gtpm.placeholder_info.click.3: {click x} -> the x position of the last click (between 0 and 1)
gtpm.placeholder_info.click.4: {click y} -> the y position of the last click (between 0 and 1)
gtpm.placeholder_info.cmd.0: Executes Minecraft commands and returns their output.
gtpm.placeholder_info.cmd.1: Requires a data item bound to a player, bind any data item to yourself by right-clicking with it.
gtpm.placeholder_info.cmp.0: Returns a 1 or 0 based on the expression in it's arguments
gtpm.placeholder_info.color.0: Returns the text from the second argument, colored with the color from the first argument. All default minecraft chat colors can be used.
gtpm.placeholder_info.combine.0: Combines all of it's arguments into a single string (by escaping all spaces between the arguments)
gtpm.placeholder_info.combine.1: Example: {combine abc def ghi jkl mno} -> "abc\ def\ ghi\ jkl\ mno"
gtpm.placeholder_info.combine.3: {combine [arg1] [arg2] [arg3] ...} -> a string that will be treated as a single argument in further placeholders
gtpm.placeholder_info.count.0: Returns how many of the provided arguments are equal to the first (compared as strings, so "0" != "0.0")
gtpm.placeholder_info.count.2: {count <arg1> [arg2] [arg3] [arg4] ...} -> the amount of arguments that are equal to the first
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.0: Stores or retrieves some data from a data item (data stick/orb/module) in one of the slots.
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.1: If you leave the <index> argument empty, it will be replaced with the value p (p is an integer from 0 to (capacity - 1) that is stored in the data item nbt).
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.3: {data get <slot> <index>} -> the data stored in the item in the specified slot
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.4: {data set <slot> <index> <value>} -> sets the data stored in the item in the specified slot, returns an empty string
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.6: {data setp <slot> <value>} -> sets p, returns an empty string
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.7: {data inc <slot>} -> increments p by 1, if p becomes more than or equal to capacity, sets p to 0
gtpm.placeholder_info.data.8: {data dec <slot>} -> decrements p by 1, if p becomes less than 0, sets p to (capacity - 1)
gtpm.placeholder_info.displayTarget.0: Returns the specified line that was transmitted to this cover using a display link.
gtpm.placeholder_info.displayTarget.2: {displayTarget <line_number>} -> the text on the specified line (line number is 1-100)
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.1: Can interact with private channels if provided with a data item bound to a player
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.10: The player_data_item_slot argument may be left empty (not 0, empty string)
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.4: {ender itemPull <channel> [player_data_item_slot]} -> pull 1 item from the ender link's buffer
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.5: {ender itemPush <channel> [player_data_item_slot]} -> push 1 item to the ender link's buffer
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.6: {ender itemId <channel> [player_data_item_slot]} -> the id of the item in the ender link's buffer (ex. "26 minecraft:dirt")
gtpm.placeholder_info.ender.9: {ender redstone <channel> <player_data_item_slot> <signal> -> sets the redstone signal outputed to the ender redstone link, returns empty string
gtpm.placeholder_info.energy.0: Returns the amount of energy stored.
gtpm.placeholder_info.energyCapacity.0: Returns the max amount of energy that can be stored
gtpm.placeholder_info.eval.0: Returns the result of evaluating the provided string which may placeholders
gtpm.placeholder_info.eval.3: {eval "repeating a: {repeat 5 \"a \"}" -> repeating a: a a a a a
gtpm.placeholder_info.eval.5: {eval "text "\""{something with spaces}"\"" more text" -> text {something with spaces} more text
gtpm.placeholder_info.fluidCount.0: Returns the amount of fluids (can be filtered).
gtpm.placeholder_info.fluidCount.2: {fluidCount [fluidId]} -> the amount of all fluids, or the fluid with fluidId if specified
gtpm.placeholder_info.formatInt.0: Returns a string representation of the provided integer
gtpm.placeholder_info.fromAscii.0: Returns the character represented by the provided ASCII code
gtpm.placeholder_info.if.0: Returns one of the arguments depending on the condition. The condition is considered true if it is not an empty string and is not equal to 0.
gtpm.placeholder_info.item.0: Returns the amount and id of the item in a specified slot
gtpm.placeholder_info.itemCount.0: Returns the amount of items (can be filtered).
gtpm.placeholder_info.itemCount.3: {itemCount <item_id>} -> amount of items with ids equal to item_id
gtpm.placeholder_info.itemCount.4: {itemCount filter <slot_id>} -> amount of items matching filter in specified slot of this cover
gtpm.placeholder_info.maintenance.0: Returns a 1 if there are maintenance problems in the block the cover is attached to, 0 otherwise.
gtpm.placeholder_info.maxProgress.0: Returns the maximum progress of the currently running recipe of the block this cover is attached to.
gtpm.placeholder_info.maxProgress.3: {maxProgress} -> the max progress of the currently running recipe
gtpm.placeholder_info.module.0: Renders the module in the specified slot onto the central monitor (does not work in a cover)
gtpm.placeholder_info.nbt.0: Returns the nbt data of the item in the specified slot
gtpm.placeholder_info.obf.0: Returns the text from the first argument, obfuscated.
gtpm.placeholder_info.previousText.0: Returns the text that was previously displayed by this cover at the specified line (before line-wrapping).
gtpm.placeholder_info.previousText.2: {previousText <line>} -> the text previously displayed on the specified line (index starts at 1)
gtpm.placeholder_info.progress.0: Returns the progress of the currently running recipe of the block this cover is attached to.
gtpm.placeholder_info.progress.1: Note that progress is an integer between 0 and {maxProgress}
gtpm.placeholder_info.progress.3: {progress} -> the progress of the currently running recipe
gtpm.placeholder_info.quad.0: Draws a quad (must specify parameters for all 4 vertices)
gtpm.placeholder_info.random.0: Returns a random number in the specified interval (inclusive).
gtpm.placeholder_info.random.2: {random <min> <max>} -> a random number between min and max (inclusive)
gtpm.placeholder_info.rect.0: Draws a rectangle at the specified position with the specified coordinates and size
gtpm.placeholder_info.rect.3: {rect 0.5 0.25 2 1 0xFFFFFFFF} -> draws a white rectangle at (0.5, 0.25) with the size (2, 1)
gtpm.placeholder_info.redstone.0: Returns the redstone signal strength or sets the redstone output strength
gtpm.placeholder_info.redstone.2: {redstone get <up|down|north|south|east|west>} -> redstone signal strength (0-15) at the specified side
gtpm.placeholder_info.redstone.3: {redstone get link <slot_index> <freq_slot_index>} -> redstone signal strength of a Create redstone link frequency specified by a linked controller in slot #slot_index. freq_slot_index is the index of the frequency inside the controller (from left to right, 0-6)
gtpm.placeholder_info.redstone.4: {redstone set <power>} -> empty string, sets the redstone output strength from this cover's side
gtpm.placeholder_info.redstone.5: {redstone set link <slot_index> <freq_slot_index> <power>} -> empty string, broadcasts the specified redstone power on the specified Create redstone link frequency
gtpm.placeholder_info.repeat.0: Returns the text from the second arguments, repeated the amount of times specified in the first argument.
gtpm.placeholder_info.repeat.2: {repeat <amount> <text>} -> text repeated the specified amount of times
gtpm.placeholder_info.select.0: Returns the argument at the specified index (starting from 0)
gtpm.placeholder_info.setImage.0: Sets the image URL in an image module in the specified slot
gtpm.placeholder_info.strike.0: Returns the text from the first text, displaying it as if it was crossed out
gtpm.placeholder_info.subList.0: Returns arguments from with indexes from l (inclusive) to r (exclusive) (starting from 0)
gtpm.placeholder_info.subList.2: {subList <left> <right> [arg0] [arg1] ...} -> all arguments with indexes from l to r separated by spaces
gtpm.placeholder_info.tick.0: Returns the amount of ticks passed from when this cover was placed.
gtpm.placeholder_info.toAscii.0: Returns the ASCII code of the provided character
gtpm.placeholder_info.toChars.0: Returns the characters of the provided string with spaces between them
gtpm.placeholder_info.toChars.1: Example: {toChars example} -> 'e x a m p l e'
gtpm.placeholder_info.underline.0: Returns the text from the first argument, underlined
gtpm.placeholder_info.voltage.0: Returns the voltage in the wire/cable the cover is on.
